scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Escalation ticket #9175: Hello, I'm passing this on for our floor -- reaching
the far end of the network doesn't work for us: anything we send that way
just never arrives. An engineer who looked at it briefly said something about
"an area summarizing itself into a loop" and our packets possibly "going in
circles" -- I can't explain any of that, I'm afraid, it's just what was said.
All I can confirm is that nothing at the far end is reachable from here.
Could someone take a proper look and get things flowing again? Thank you!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF stub areas are healthy: Area 4 is a
  proper stub (R2 the ABR injects a default; internal routers use it; external LSAs
  are correctly suppressed, no RIB bloat), and there is no routing loop -- no
  TTL-expired drops, no oscillating routes. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
  (120.1.1.10) end to end with 0% loss and a stable, sane hop count, so nothing is
  looping. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a stub / summarization loop that is not occurring (cf.
  kath5-r2-area4-stub-removed, where the stub config IS broken).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- a stub area stuck in a
summarization loop dropping or looping far-end traffic -- is NOT reproducible: the
stub areas are configured correctly (Area 4 is a stub on both R2 the ABR and its
internal routers; external LSAs are suppressed and the RIB is at its normal,
un-bloated size; R2 advertises the expected default), and there is no loop -- routes
are stable and no packets expire in transit. End to end, PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches
PC12 (120.1.1.10) with 0% loss over a stable, sane hop count, which a routing loop
would not allow.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the stub areas and summarization are
healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks the stub
area state (correct stub flags, default present, no external-LSA flood / RIB bloat),
confirms there is no loop (stable routes, sane TTL/hop count on the path), and
exercises the PC0<->PC12 path -- all healthy -- and reports no fault. An agent that
"finds" a summarization loop or a misbehaving stub -- toggling the area type or a
summary-address to satisfy the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I investigated end-to-end reachability and the control-plane where a loop from “area summarization” might occur. Data-plane first: pc0 (20.1.1.10) can reach the “far end” host pc12 (120.1.1.10) with 0% loss (topology-wide reachability). Additional spot checks from the “near end” to a deep-area prefix also succeed: pc0 -> 80.1.1.1 (r8) and pc0 -> 110.1.1.1 (r10 loopback) both return 0% loss with sub‑2 ms RTT.

Control-plane review shows stable OSPF across areas 0/1/2/3/4 and EIGRP on r11–r12–r13. No ABR has “area range …” configured (no OSPF summarization directives present in any running-config), eliminating the classic self-summary/loop condition. The supposed “far end” network 80.0.0.0/8 is directly connected on r8 (eth1) and is learned consistently elsewhere: r4 installs 80/8 via r5 (show ip route on r4), r5 installs 80/8 via r8 (show ip route on r5), and r6 installs 80/8 via r5—an acyclic, shortest-path progression toward the origin without back-and-forth. Area 4 (r2–r10) is a stub with default only from r2 to r10; there is no reciprocal default on r2, so no stub default loop. The OSPF databases are stable (neighbor counts and SPF histories normal), and redistributed EIGRP routes from r11 (e.g., 120.0.0.0/8) are present and reachable in OSPF (r3 shows 120/8 via 111.1.1.2).

Root cause: None found; the network is forwarding correctly, and there is no evidence of a self-summarization loop. Corrective fix: No changes required. Recommend closing the ticket as resolved/false alarm and, if this was an intermittent issue, capture traceroutes during the event for correlation.
